targetAudience.primary: Agent API and control-plane engineers responsible for compatibility and authorization boundaries
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands permissive request schemas, API migration and basic authorization semantics.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A retired request field can disappear silently under forward-compatible decoding even when that disappearance changes the caller's security expectation.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex app-server change demonstrates a narrow mechanism that preserves general unknown-field tolerance while rejecting one obsolete permission field before permissive decoding.

externalHook.description: The same unknown-field tolerance that enables forward compatibility can erase security-significant intent when a retired field is silently ignored.

coreProposition: Forward-compatible agent APIs should preserve general unknown-field tolerance while explicitly rejecting retired fields whose silent loss would change authorization or execution meaning.

originalValue.description: Separates structural schema compatibility from authorization-semantic compatibility and turns that distinction into a bounded retirement decision rule.

readerTakeaway: Classify retired fields by semantic risk, reject dangerous removals before permissive decoding, provide a migration path and keep the failure request-local when possible.

supported: One merged implementation rejects permissionProfile on four app-server methods before permissive deserialization.
Unrelated unknown fields remain accepted, named permissions remain usable and rejection does not poison the connection.
unsupported: Complete coverage of every permission-bearing path
uncertain: Which future field retirements warrant the same fail-closed exception
How stale-client telemetry should be governed

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article's value and argument concern general agent API governance and do not depend on any first-party project.

decisionReason: The same-day primary implementation evidence supports a narrow mechanism, while the Research Object supplies an original and explicitly bounded compatibility-governance judgment.
